source_title: Life Time Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
source_excerpt:
Total revenue of $893.5 million increased 14.2% over the prior year quarter
Net income of $106.5 million increased 4.0% over the prior year quarter
Diluted EPS of $0.46 increased 2.2% over the prior year quarter
Adjusted net income of $115.9 million increased 24.6% over the prior year quarter
Adjusted EBITDA of $256.3 million increased 16.5% over the prior year quarter
Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.51 increased 24.4% over the prior year quarter
CHANHASSEN, Minn. , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Life Time Group Holdings, Inc. ("Life Time," "we," "our," "us," or the "Company") (NYSE: LTH ) today announced its financial results for the fiscal third quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Bahram Akradi, Founder, Chairman and CEO, stated: "Our third quarter results reflect our continued delivery of exceptional member experiences and the strength of our brand. Member engagement continues to rise and our in-center businesses are performing very well, resulting in higher revenue per membership. We are on track to open all 14 new clubs planned for this year, and nearly all of our clubs planned for 2027 are already under construction. With our low leverage, strong cash flow and robust real estate pipeline, we are well positioned for long-term growth."
($ in millions, except for Average center
The three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 included non-cash share-based compensation expense of $13.9 million and $14.9 million, respectively. The nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 included non-cash share-based compensation expense of $36.9 million and $39.4 million, respectively.
The Company includes a center, for comparable center revenue purposes, beginning on the first day of the 13th full calendar month of the center's operation, in order to assess the center's growth rate after one year of operation.
Revenue increased 14.2% to $893.5 million due to continued strong growth in membership dues and in-center revenue, driven by an increase in average dues including from improved membership mix, membership growth in our new and ramping centers and higher member utilization of our in-center offerings, particularly in Dynamic Personal Training.
Center memberships of 858,747 increased by 18,125, or 2.2%, when compared to September 30, 2025, due to continued improvement in membership mix, including an approximately 21,500 reduction in qualified memberships administered through medical insurance providers, which have significantly lower average dues, and decreased by 1,294, or (0.2%), from June 30, 2026, consistent with seasonality expectations.
Total subscriptions, which include center memberships and on-hold memberships, of 908,454 increased 1.9% compared to September 30, 2025.
Center operations expenses increased 14.5% to $474.5 million primarily due to operating costs related to our new and ramping centers, additional center operating expenses related to increased club utilization in our mature centers, as well as costs to support in-center business revenue growth.
General, administrative and marketing expenses increased 10.0% to $65.8 million primarily due to increases in incentive and benefit-related expenses and marketing costs.
Net income increased 4.0% to $106.5 million primarily due to business performance, as well as a tax-effected net gain of $2.3 million on a sale-leaseback transaction. Net income in the prior year period included tax-effected net cash proceeds of $16.2 million received from employee retention credits under the CARES Act, and a tax-effected net gain of $5.7 million on a sale-leaseback transaction.
Adjusted net income increased 24.6% to $115.9 million and Adjusted EBITDA increased 16.5% to $256.3 million as we experienced greater flow through of our increased revenue.
Revenue increased 13.2% to $2,548.2 million due to continued strong growth in membership dues and in-center revenue, driven by an increase in average dues including from improved membership mix, membership growth in our new and ramping centers and higher member utilization of our in-center offerings, particularly in Dynamic Personal Training.
Center operations expenses increased 12.3% to $1,335.0 million primarily due to operating costs related to our new and ramping centers, additional center operating expenses related to increased club utilization in our mature centers, as well as costs to support in-center business revenue growth.
General, administrative and marketing expenses increased 6.7% to $191.4 million primarily due to increases in incentive and benefit-related expenses, increases in center support overhead to enhance and broaden our member services and experiences and increased marketing costs.
Net income increased 18.0% to $295.9 million primarily due to business performance, as well as tax-effected net gains of $3.8 million on sale-leaseback transactions and tax-effected net cash proceeds of $3.7 million received in partial satisfaction of legal claims. Net income in the prior year period included tax-effected net cash proceeds of $27.2 million received from employee retention credits under the CARES Act and $12.6 million of income tax benefits due to a significant exercise of stock options by our Chief Executive Officer that were set to expire in 2025, partially offset by a tax-effected net loss of $3.8 million on sale-leaseback transactions.
Adjusted net income increased 28.1% to $321.9 million and Adjusted EBITDA increased 17.2% to $729.4 million as we experienced greater flow through of our increased revenue.
We opened one new center during the third quarter of 2026.
As of September 30, 2026, we operated a total of 196 centers.
Net cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $670.5 million, an increase of 6.3% compared to the prior year period. The prior year period included certain non-recurring items, primarily related to tax-effected net cash proceeds of $27.2 million received from employee retention credits under the CARES Act.
We completed one sale-leaseback transaction for one property and net proceeds of $62.3 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we have completed three sale-leaseback transactions for six properties and total net proceeds of $262.5 million.
Our capital expenditures by type of expenditure were as follows:
Consist of new center land and construction, initial major remodels of acquired centers, major remodels of existing centers that expand existing square footage, asset acquisitions including the purchase of previously leased centers and other growth initiatives.
Consist of capital expenditures required to maintain the operating condition of our existing centers.
Consist of capital expenditures related to updates and enhancements to our existing centers, technology investments, and corporate infrastructure.
Our net debt leverage ratio improved to 1.3 times as of September 30, 2026, from 1.6 times as of September 30, 2025.
As of September 30, 2026, our total available liquidity was $919.1 million, which included $632.9 million of availability on our $650.0 million revolving credit facility and $286.2 million of cash and cash equivalents. At September 30, 2026, there were no outstanding borrowings under our revolving credit facility and there were $17.1 million of outstanding letters of credit.
The Company is reiterating the following expectations for fiscal 2026 as outlined in its second quarter 2026 results announced on July 30, 2026:
Open 14 new clubs, most of which will be large-format, ground-up construction clubs. We expect the total square footage of our 2026 class of clubs to be approximately 1.3 million square feet, nearly double the square footage of each of our 2024 class and 2025 class of clubs. We have opened seven new clubs as of September 30, 2026, and we opened one additional new club in October 2026. We expect to open the remaining six in the fourth quarter of 2026.
Complete approximately $135 million in additional sale-leaseback transactions during the fourth quarter of 2026 for a total of approximately $400 million during the fiscal year.
Maintenance capital expenditures of $140 million to $150 million, modernization and technology capital expenditures of $140 million to $150 million, and growth capital expenditures of $885 million to $910 million.
Provision for income tax rate estimate of 27%.
Manage our net debt to Adjusted EBITDA leverage ratio to maintain at or below 2.00 times.
The Company is also updating the following operational and financial expectations for fiscal 2026:
Comparable center revenue growth of 8.5% to 8.7%, which includes our ramping and mature centers, increased from 7.9% to 8.3%.
Interest expense, net of interest income, of approximately $59 million to $62 million, and net of $27 million to $29 million of capitalized interest expense related to construction in progress, tightened from $59 million to $63 million and lowered from $28 million to $30 million, respectively.
Rent to include non-cash rent expense of $33 million to $35 million, tightened from $32 million to $35 million.
Cash income tax expense of $82 million to $83 million, decreased from $103 million to $105 million primarily due to higher projected tax depreciation, a net operating loss deduction carryforward from 2025, and a larger 2025 federal overpayment applied to 2026 than expected.
Full year net income to include the impact of net losses associated with sale-leaseback transactions.
Year-end weighted-average diluted common shares outstanding of approximately 228 million to 229 million, not including any incremental impact that may occur as a result of our $500 million share buyback program, tightened from 227 million to 229 million.

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Key Performance Indicators
This press release includes certain financial measures that are not presented in accordance with GAAP, including Adjusted net income, Adjusted net income per common share, Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and net debt and ratios and calculations with respect thereto. These non-GAAP financial measures are not based on any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles and should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for or superior to, net income, net income per common share, net cash provided by operating activities or total debt (defined as long-term debt, net of current portion, plus current maturities of debt) as a measure of financial performance or liquidity or any other performance measure derived in accordance with GAAP, and should not be construed as an inference that the Company's future results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items. In addition, these non-GAAP financial measures should be read in conjunction with the Company's financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. The reconciliations of the Company's non-GAAP financial measures to the corresponding GAAP measures should be carefully evaluated.
Adjusted net income is defined as net income excluding the impact of share-based compensation expense as well as (gain) loss on sale-leaseback transactions, capital transaction costs, legal settlements, asset impairment, severance and other items that are not indicative of our ongoing operations, less the tax effect of these adjustments. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income before interest expense, net, provision for income taxes and depreciation and amortization, excluding the impact of share-based compensation expense as well as (gain) loss on sale-leaseback transactions, capital transaction costs, legal settlements, asset impairment, severance and other items that are not indicative of the Company's ongoing operations. Free cash flow is defined as net cash provided by operating activities less capital expenditures, net of construction reimbursements, plus net proceeds from sale-leaseback transactions and land sales. Net debt is defined as long-term debt, net of current portion, plus current maturities of debt, excluding fair value adjustments, unamortized debt discounts and issuance costs, minus cash and cash equivalents. Net debt is as of the last day of the respective quarter or year. Our leverage ratio is calculated as our net debt divided by our trailing twelve months of Adjusted EBITDA.
The Company presents these non-GAAP financial measures because management believes that these measures assist investors and analysts in comparing the Company's operating performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that management does not believe are indicative of the Company's ongoing operating performance, and management believes that free cash flow assists investors and analysts in evaluating our liquidity and cash flows, including our ability to make principal payments on our indebtedness and to fund our capital expenditures and working capital requirements. Investors are encouraged to evaluate these adjustments and the reasons the Company considers them appropriate for supplemental analysis. In evaluating the non-GAAP financial measures, investors should be aware that, in the future, the Company may incur expenses that are the same as or similar to some of the adjustments in the Company's presentation of its non-GAAP financial measures. There can be no assurance that the Company will not modify the presentation of non-GAAP financial measures in future periods, and any such modification may be material. In addition, the Company's non-GAAP financial measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies in the Company's industry or across different industries.
The non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical tools, and investors should not consider these measures in isolation or as substitutes for analysis of the Company's results as reported under GAAP.

We define Average Center revenue per center membership as Center revenue less On-hold revenue, divided by the average number of Center memberships for the period, where the average number of Center memberships for the period is an average derived from dividing the sum of the total Center memberships outstanding at the beginning of the period and at the end of each month during the period by one plus the number of months in each period.
We measure the results of our centers based on how long each center has been open as of the most recent measurement period. We include a center, for comparable center revenue purposes, beginning on the first day of the 13th full calendar month of the center's operation, in order to assess the center's growth rate after one year of operation.
Net new center openings is calculated as the number of centers that opened for the first time to members during the period, less any centers that closed during the period. Total centers (end of period) is the number of centers operational as of the last day of the period. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, we opened one center.
Total center square footage (end of period) reflects the aggregate square footage, excluding the areas used for tennis courts, outdoor swimming pools, outdoor play areas and stand-alone Work, Sport and Swim locations. We use this metric for evaluating the efficiencies of a center as of the end of the period. These figures are approximations.
Net income margin is calculated as net income divided by total revenue.
We present Adjusted net income as a supplemental measure of our performance. We define Adjusted net income as net income excluding the impact of share-based compensation expense as well as (gain) loss on sale-leaseback transactions, capital transaction costs, legal settlements, asset impairment, severance and other items that are not indicative of our ongoing operations, less the tax effect of these adjustments.
Adjusted net income margin is calculated as Adjusted net income divided by total revenue.
